scenarioStory.history: Daughter reports patient was talking normally about 40 minutes ago, then developed slurred speech and a droopy left side of her face. Daughter stepped out of the room briefly and returned to find the patient vomiting on the couch and no longer responding to her name or voice, only withdrawing slightly to a sternal rub.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 68-year-old female supine on the couch, unresponsive to voice, with visible emesis and gurgling respirations. Left facial droop and right-sided flaccid hemiparesis are noted on primary survey. → Airway suctioned, preoxygenated for RSI: Crew suctions the oropharynx, completes a rapid stroke assessment (LKW time, stroke scale, BGL), and performs RSI to protect the airway given the patient's loss of protective reflexes and active vomiting. → Tube confirmed and stroke alert transmitted: Patient is intubated, sedated, and ventilated with continuous waveform capnography. Early stroke center notification has been transmitted and the patient is positioned with head of stretcher elevated to reduce aspiration risk during transport.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Altered mental status, found vomiting and unresponsive to voice

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 68-year-old female supine on the couch, unresponsive to voice, with visible emesis and gurgling respirations. Left facial droop and right-sided flaccid hemiparesis are noted on primary survey.
relatedChecklist: Suction oropharynx immediately to clear emesis and reduce aspiration risk
Perform validated stroke scale and determine last known well time
Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a stroke mimic
Recognize loss of protective airway reflexes; proceed to RSI for airway protection
Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive pressure ventilation for at least 2 minutes before RSI

scenarioEvents.name: Airway suctioned, preoxygenated for RSI
scenarioEvents.description: Crew suctions the oropharynx, completes a rapid stroke assessment (LKW time, stroke scale, BGL), and performs RSI to protect the airway given the patient's loss of protective reflexes and active vomiting.
relatedChecklist: Etomidate 21 mg IV push (70 kg × 0.3 mg/kg) as induction agent
Succinylcholine 105 mg IV push (70 kg × 1.5 mg/kg) as paralytic agent
Confirm ET tube placement with waveform capnography, breath sounds, and absent gastric sounds
Transmit early stroke center notification for suspected large vessel occlusion

scenarioEvents.name: Tube confirmed and stroke alert transmitted
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is intubated, sedated, and ventilated with continuous waveform capnography. Early stroke center notification has been transmitted and the patient is positioned with head of stretcher elevated to reduce aspiration risk during transport.
relatedChecklist: Elevate head of stretcher 15-30 degrees, maintain neutral neck alignment during transport

scenarioEvents.name: Suctioning and RSI delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew prioritizes history-taking and the stroke scale without first clearing the airway. The patient vomits again and aspirates before suction or RSI is initiated, worsening oxygenation.
relatedChecklist: Immediately suction airway and prepare for emergent RSI given worsening hypoxia
